title: Common model erases provider-specific capability required for correctness
task: Review a provider-normalization layer that converts two storage providers into one lowest-common-denominator object.
context: Provider A exposes strong conditional-write semantics.
Provider B does not provide the same guarantee.
The normalized model represents both providers as supporting a generic write operation.
Callers rely on conditional writes to prevent lost updates.
evidence: The normalization layer drops the capability distinction.
One caller now performs the same write path for both providers.
Provider B can violate the caller's lost-update invariant under concurrency.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Keep the uniform model because provider differences should always be hidden.
Emulate the guarantee silently even though no correct implementation is available.
expected_decision_properties: Recognize that the provider difference is domain-relevant rather than incidental.
Preserve or expose the capability distinction explicitly.
Prevent callers from assuming semantics a provider cannot guarantee.
Keep normalization for truly incidental differences where it remains useful.
unacceptable_reasoning: A clean abstraction must make all providers look identical.
Provider-specific capabilities should never appear in an application model.
expected_tradeoffs: simple caller API vs explicit capability handling
verification_expectations: Add capability-aware tests for both providers.
Verify callers cannot invoke conditional semantics when unsupported.
specialist_boundary: Exact storage consistency/conditional-write guarantees require provider/database-specific verification.
